extracted.intended_audience: readers of Charles Lamb; literary enthusiasts and correspondents
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted evaluative guidance and stylistic observations embedded in Charles Lamb's letters (about poetry, narrative technique, handwriting, and authors' livelihoods). Useful for understanding 19th-century informal standards for literary taste and epistolary presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid slang and excessive provincialism in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: In poetry _slang_ of every kind is to be avoided. There is a rustic Cockneyism, as little pleasing as ours of London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local or rustic phrases sparingly: "Now and then a home rusticism is fresh and startling; but when nothing is gained in expression, it is out of tenor. It may make folks smile and stare; but the ungenial coalition of barbarous with refined phrases will prevent you in the end from being so generally tasted as you desire to be." Model: Shenstone's 'true rustic style.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Value acute observation in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for Clare: "The quality of your observation has astonished me."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close, accurate observation of local scenes and particulars (e.g., 'Recollections after a Ramble', 'Grongar Hill') is a primary source of poetic strength; such observation is singled out as what most pleases the critic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider whether dialect authenticates or merely startles
rubrics_metrics.description: Question posed: "Would his 'School-mistress,' the prettiest of poems, have been better if he had used quite the Goody's own language?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using dialect, ask whether it adds genuine expressive value or merely novelty; authenticity alone isn't sufficient—dialect should serve the poem's tone and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create verisimilitude with matter-of-fact detail
rubrics_metrics.description: On Defoe: "In the appearance of _truth,_ in all the incidents and conversations that occur in them, they exceed any works of fiction I am acquainted with. It is perfect illusion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ minute, documentary detail (dates, log-book precision, court-evidence tone) to produce an impression of truth. Techniques include pain-staking detail, narrative impartiality, and the repetition of facts to reinforce credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain narrator-credibility; avoid intrusive authorial presence
rubrics_metrics.description: "The author never appears in these self-narratives (for so they ought to be called), but the narrator chains us down to an implicit belief in everything he says."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the story through a consistent narrator persona rather than frequent authorial asides; let the narrator's voice and methodical detail secure reader belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt diction to the intended audience (plain and homely for popular appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defoe's style: "everywhere beautiful, but plain and _homely._ 'Robinson Crusoe' is delightful to all ranks and classes; but it is easy to see that it is written in phraseology peculiarly adapted to the lower conditions of readers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose phrasing and level of rhetorical polish to fit readership: plain, homely language can broaden accessibility and suit particular audiences (seafaring men, servant-maids, poor boys), while still being artistically valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overlong relations of mundane incidents unless they serve more than verisimilitude
rubrics_metrics.description: "His passion for _matter-of-fact narrative_ sometimes betrayed him into a long relation of common incidents, which might happen to any man, and have no interest but the intense appearance of truth in them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long, merely documentary passages risk boring readers; ensure that extended anecdotal material contributes narrative interest or thematic import beyond simply proving reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use repetition strategically to impress truth upon readers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Facts are repeated over and over in varying phrases, till you cannot choose but believe them. ... he _repeats_ it with his favorite figure of speech, 'I say' so and so"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repetition of facts or motives (in varied phrasing) can be an effective rhetorical device to fix details in the reader's mind and strengthen the illusion of authenticity—especially with audiences attuned to matter-of-fact testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter presentation: prefer neat, confident handwriting and a fair copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mary's handwriting: "There is an essential poverty and abjectness in the frame of them. They look like begging letters. And then she is sure to omit a most substantial word in the second draught (for she never ventures an epistle without a foul copy first), which is obliged to be interlined,--which spoils the neatest epistle... Her figures ... are not figures, but figurantes; and the combined posse go staggering up and down shameless, as drunkards in the daytime. Her lines 'are not less erring' than her words; a sort of unnatural parallel lines, that are perpetually threatening to meet,--which, you know, is quite contrary to Euclid. Her very blots are not bold ... but poor smears, half left in and half scratched out."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a clean fair copy for correspondence: avoid sloppy, 'begging'-looking penmanship; don't omit words that force interlineations; keep numerals and ruled lines regular; write boldly and confidently rather than leaving faint smears—presentation affects perceived character and seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career advice for authors: avoid dependence on booksellers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Throw yourself on the world without any rational plan of support beyond what the chance employ of booksellers would afford you!... They are Turks and Tartars when they have poor authors at their beck... I contend that a bookseller has a _relative honesty_ towards authors, not like his honesty to the rest of the world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a stable salaried employment (e.g., banking/office posts) over relying solely on bookselling income; financial security preserves time, independence, and mental freedom for writing rather than drudgery or exploitation.
